title: The Science Fair Surprise
summary: A girl's volcano project fails during a rehearsal the night before the science fair, so she and her brother test the mixture, find the problem, and fix it just in time.
poll: Making mistakes while working on a project is a bad thing.

versions.title: The Science Fair Surprise
versions.text:
Layla had a fair at school. It was the next day.

She made a toy volcano. She wanted a big show.

That night, she did a test. Her brother Omar was there too. She poured in the mix. She hoped for a big blast. But just a few bubbles came up. It did not work.

Layla felt sad. "Let's check your notes," said Omar. They read the card again. Layla saw the problem. She put in too little soda.

They tried again. This time she used more soda. She poured it in. Red bubbles shot up and over the top! It worked!

Layla wrote down the right mixture. Omar helped her clean up. Then they went to bed.

The next day, Layla set up her volcano. She poured in the mix. It went off big and red! Her class cheered. Layla had found the problem. She had fixed it too.

versions.title: The Science Fair Surprise
versions.text:
Layla had a science fair at school tomorrow. She had made a model volcano. She wanted it to work well.

That night, Layla and Omar did a test. They were in the kitchen. She poured in the mix. She waited for a big eruption. Only a few weak bubbles came up. It did not work at all.

Layla felt very sad. "Let's check your notes," said Omar. They looked at the card again. Layla soon saw the problem. She had used too little soda.

They tried again. This time, Layla put in much more soda. Red, fizzy bubbles rushed up. They spilled over the sides! It finally worked.

Layla quickly wrote down the right mixture. She did not want to forget it. Omar helped her clean up the table. Then they went to bed.

The next day, Layla set up her volcano at the fair. She poured in the mix. It erupted big and red, just as she had hoped! Her classmates cheered loudly. Layla had found the problem, and she had fixed it.

versions.title: The Science Fair Surprise
versions.text:
Layla had a science fair at school the next day. She had spent weeks on her model volcano. She wanted everything to work well.

That evening, Layla and her brother Omar did a test run in the kitchen. She poured the mixture into the volcano. She waited for a huge eruption. Instead, only a few weak bubbles came out. The volcano barely worked at all.

Layla felt sad and a bit worried. "Let's check your notes," said Omar, trying to help. They looked at the card together. After a moment, Layla spotted the problem. She had used far too little soda.

They tried the test again. This time, Layla put in much more soda before pouring in the rest of the mix. Red, fizzy bubbles rushed up at once. They spilled over the sides of the volcano! It finally worked the way she had hoped.

Layla quickly wrote down the right mixture. She wanted to remember it for the next day. Omar helped her clean up the table. They both went to bed feeling much more sure of themselves.

The next day, Layla set up her volcano at the fair. She poured in the mixture she had tested the night before. It erupted big and red, just as she had hoped! Her classmates cheered loudly. Layla had found a problem, tried a fix, and made it work.

versions.title: The Science Fair Surprise
versions.text:
Layla had a science fair the next morning. She had spent weeks on a model volcano for her project. She wanted it to work well in front of her class and the judges.

That evening, Layla and her brother Omar did a rehearsal in the kitchen. Carefully, she poured the mixture into the volcano. She waited for a huge eruption. Instead, only a few weak bubbles came out of the top. The volcano barely worked, and Layla's heart sank.

Layla felt sad and more than a little worried. There was no time left to start over. "Let's check your notes," said Omar, trying to help his sister stay calm. They looked at the recipe card together, step by step. After a moment, Layla spotted the problem. She had measured far too little baking soda for the vinegar she used.

They decided to try the test again, right away. This time, Layla measured out much more baking soda. Then she poured in the vinegar. Red, fizzy bubbles rushed up at once. They spilled over the sides of the volcano! It finally worked just as she had hoped.

Layla quickly wrote down the right mixture. She wanted to remember it for the real day. Omar helped her clean up the table, and the two of them went to bed feeling far more sure of themselves.

The next day, Layla set up her volcano at the fair. She poured in the same mixture she had tested the night before. It erupted big and red, just as she had hoped! Her classmates cheered loudly, and the judges smiled too. Layla had found a problem, tried a fix, and made it work.

versions.title: The Science Fair Surprise
versions.text:
Imagine spending weeks on a project. Then it fails the night before it really matters. That is what happened to Layla.

Layla had built a model volcano for her school science fair. The fair was happening the next morning. She had mixed baking soda, vinegar, and red food coloring. She wanted it to look like real lava.

That evening, Layla and her brother Omar held a rehearsal in the kitchen. She poured the mixture into the volcano. She waited for a huge eruption. Instead, only a few weak bubbles came out. The result was nothing like what she had hoped for.

Layla felt worried, since there was almost no time left before the fair. "Let's check your notes," Omar said, trying to keep his sister calm. They looked at each ingredient on the recipe card, line by line. After a moment, Layla saw the problem. The ratio of soda to vinegar was wrong. She had used far too little soda.

Determined to fix it, they repeated the whole process again. This time, Layla measured out more soda before pouring in the vinegar. Red, fizzy bubbles rushed up at once. They spilled over the sides of the volcano. The test finally worked just as she had pictured it.

Relieved, Layla wrote down the right mixture. She did not want to forget it for the real day. Omar helped her clean up the kitchen, and they went to bed feeling far more sure of themselves.

The next morning, Layla set up her volcano at the fair. She poured in the same mixture she had tested the night before. It erupted big and red in front of her class and the judges, just as she had hoped. Everyone cheered. Her teacher praised her for finding a problem, testing a fix, and trying again. That, her teacher said, is how real scientists work.

versions.title: The Science Fair Surprise
versions.text:
Imagine spending weeks on a project. Then it fails the night before it really matters. That is exactly what happened to Layla.

Layla had built a model volcano out of cardboard and clay for her school science fair. The fair was set for the next morning. Her plan was to mix baking soda, vinegar, and red food coloring to make a reaction that looked like real lava.

That evening, Layla and her brother Omar held a rehearsal in the kitchen. They wanted to make sure everything was ready. She poured the mixture into the volcano and waited for a big eruption. Instead, only a few weak bubbles came out, and the result looked nothing like what she had pictured.

Layla felt worried, since there was almost no time left before the fair began. "Let's check your notes," Omar said calmly, trying to keep his sister from panicking. Together, they looked at the recipe card line by line, checking each ingredient and amount she had written down. After a moment, Layla noticed the problem. The ratio of baking soda to vinegar was wrong. She had measured far too little soda for the vinegar she had poured.

Determined to fix it, the two of them repeated the whole process. This time, Layla measured out a much larger amount of baking soda. Then she slowly poured in the vinegar. Red, fizzy bubbles rushed up at once and spilled over the sides of the volcano, just as she had pictured. The test had finally worked.

Relieved and a little proud, Layla wrote down the right mixture so she would not forget it before the real day. Omar helped her clean up the kitchen table, and they went to bed feeling far more sure of themselves than an hour before.

The next morning, Layla set up her volcano at the fair. She poured in the same mixture she had tested the night before. It erupted big and bright red in front of her class and the judges, just as she had hoped. Everyone cheered, and her teacher praised her for noticing a problem, testing a fix, and trying again without giving up.

versions.title: The Science Fair Surprise
versions.text:
Imagine spending several weeks on a science project, only to watch it completely fail the night before it really mattered. That is exactly what happened to Layla.

Layla had built a model volcano out of cardboard and clay for her school science fair, which was set for the next morning. Her plan was to mix baking soda, vinegar, and red food coloring to create a reaction that would look like real lava erupting from the mountain.

That evening, Layla and her brother Omar held a careful rehearsal in the kitchen, wanting to make sure everything was ready before the real event. She poured the mixture into the volcano and waited for a huge eruption. Instead, only a few weak bubbles came out, and the result looked nothing like what she had imagined.

Layla felt disappointed and worried, since there was almost no time left before the fair began. "Let's check your notes together," Omar said calmly, trying to keep his sister from panicking under the pressure. Together, they reviewed the recipe card line by line, checking each amount she had written down, until Layla noticed the problem. The ratio of baking soda to vinegar was wrong, since she had measured far too little soda for the vinegar she had poured.

Determined to fix the mistake, the two of them repeated the process right away. This time, Layla measured out a much larger amount of baking soda before slowly pouring in the vinegar, and red, fizzy bubbles rushed up at once and spilled over the sides of the volcano, just as she had pictured. The test had finally worked.

Relieved and a little proud, Layla wrote down the right mixture so she would not forget it before the real day. Omar helped her clean up the table, and they went to bed feeling far more sure of themselves than they had an hour before.

The next morning, Layla set up her volcano at the fair and poured in the same mixture she had tested the night before. It erupted big and bright red in front of her classmates and the judges, just as she had hoped, and her teacher praised her for noticing a problem, testing a fix, and trying again.

Later, a judge asked Layla what she had learned from the whole experience. She explained that scientists often fail several times before finding the right answer, and that changing even one small part, like the amount of an ingredient, can completely change the result. Her honest answer impressed the judges as much as the eruption itself had.

versions.title: The Science Fair Surprise
versions.text:
Few experiences are more stressful than watching a project fail the night before it truly matters, which is exactly what happened to Layla.

Layla had spent weeks constructing a model volcano from cardboard and clay for her school's science fair, scheduled for the next morning. Her plan involved combining baking soda, vinegar, and red food coloring to produce a reaction that would resemble molten lava.

That evening, Layla and her brother Omar conducted a rehearsal in the kitchen, hoping to confirm that everything worked before the real presentation. She poured the mixture into the volcano and waited, expecting a dramatic eruption. Instead, only a handful of weak bubbles trickled out, bearing little resemblance to what she had pictured.

Disappointed and increasingly anxious, since almost no time remained before the fair, Layla nearly gave up. "Let's analyze your notes," Omar suggested calmly, hoping to keep his sister from panicking. Together, they examined the recipe card line by line, comparing each ingredient against the quantities she had recorded. Layla then identified the problem: the ratio between baking soda and vinegar, the one variable she had changed, was entirely wrong.

Determined to correct the mistake, the siblings repeated the process, forming a clearer hypothesis about the right proportions. Layla calculated a larger quantity of baking soda and slowly poured in the vinegar. Red, fizzy bubbles erupted upward at once and spilled over the sides of the volcano, precisely as she had pictured. Her persistence had finally paid off.

Relieved and quietly proud, Layla recorded the correct mixture so she would not forget it before the real presentation. Omar helped her tidy the kitchen, and the two of them went to bed feeling considerably more confident than an hour earlier.

The next morning, Layla assembled her volcano at the fair and poured in the mixture she had successfully tested the night before. It erupted boldly in front of her classmates and the judges, exactly as she had hoped. Her teacher praised her for recognizing a problem, testing a solution, and persisting without giving up.

Later, a judge asked Layla what she had learned from the experience. She explained that scientists frequently fail several times before discovering the correct answer, and that adjusting even a single variable, such as the ratio of ingredients, can completely transform the outcome.

versions.title: The Science Fair Surprise
versions.text:
Few experiences are more stressful than watching a carefully planned project fail on the night before it truly matters. That is precisely what happened to Layla.

Layla had spent several weeks constructing a model volcano from cardboard and clay for her school's science fair. It was scheduled for the following morning. Her plan involved combining baking soda, vinegar, and red food coloring to produce a reaction that would closely resemble molten lava.

That evening, Layla and her brother Omar conducted a thorough rehearsal in the kitchen. They wanted to confirm that everything worked before the real presentation. She poured the mixture into the volcano and waited, anticipating a dramatic eruption. Instead, only a handful of weak, unimpressive bubbles trickled out, bearing almost no resemblance to what she had envisioned.

Disappointed and increasingly anxious, since almost no time remained before the fair began, Layla nearly considered giving up. "Let's analyze your notes together," Omar suggested calmly, hoping to keep his sister from panicking under the pressure. Together, they examined the recipe card line by line, comparing each ingredient against the exact quantities she had recorded. Layla finally identified the problem: the ratio between baking soda and vinegar, the one variable she had unintentionally changed, was entirely incorrect.

Determined to correct the mistake before it was too late, the siblings repeated the process, forming a clearer hypothesis about the correct proportions. Layla calculated a noticeably larger quantity of baking soda before slowly pouring in the vinegar. Red, fizzy bubbles erupted upward immediately and spilled dramatically over the sides of the volcano, precisely as she had imagined. Her persistence, it seemed, had finally paid off.

Relieved and quietly proud, Layla carefully recorded the correct mixture so she would not forget it before the real presentation. Omar helped her tidy up the kitchen, and the two of them went to bed feeling considerably more confident than an hour earlier.

The next morning, Layla assembled her volcano at the science fair and poured in the same mixture she had successfully tested the night before. It erupted boldly in front of her classmates and the judges, exactly as she had hoped. Her teacher praised her warmly for recognizing a problem, testing a solution, and persisting without giving up.

Later, a judge asked Layla what she had personally learned from the experience. She explained thoughtfully that scientists frequently fail several times before discovering the correct answer, and that adjusting even a single variable, such as the ratio of ingredients, can completely transform the final outcome.

versions.title: The Science Fair Surprise
versions.text:
Few experiences prove as unsettling as watching a meticulously planned project collapse on the very night before it truly matters, which is precisely the predicament in which Layla suddenly found herself. She had spent several weeks constructing a model volcano from cardboard and clay for her school's annual science fair, intending to combine baking soda, vinegar, and red food coloring into a chemical reaction that would convincingly resemble molten lava erupting from the mountain's summit.

That evening, Layla and her younger brother Omar conducted a rehearsal in the kitchen, determined to confirm that every component of the experiment functioned correctly before the actual presentation the following morning. She poured the mixture into the volcano and waited, anticipating a dramatic eruption; instead, only a handful of weak, unimpressive bubbles trickled out, bearing almost no resemblance to the spectacle she had envisioned. Disappointed and increasingly anxious, since scarcely any time remained before the fair began, Layla nearly considered abandoning the project altogether.

"Let's systematically analyze your notes," Omar suggested calmly, hoping to prevent his sister from succumbing to panic under the mounting pressure. Together, they examined the recipe card line by line, meticulously comparing each ingredient against the quantities she had originally recorded, until Layla finally identified the problem: the ratio between baking soda and vinegar, the one variable she had unintentionally altered, was entirely incorrect, since she had measured far too little baking soda relative to the generous amount of vinegar she had poured.

Determined to correct the mistake before it became irreversible, the siblings repeated the entire process, this time forming a clearer hypothesis regarding the correct proportions. Layla calculated a considerably larger quantity of baking soda before slowly pouring in the vinegar, and red, fizzy bubbles erupted upward immediately, spilling dramatically over the sides exactly as she had always imagined. Her persistence, it seemed, had finally been rewarded, and relieved as well as quietly proud, she carefully recorded the correct mixture so as not to forget it before the real presentation.

The following morning, Layla assembled her volcano at the science fair and poured in the very mixture she had successfully tested the night before. It erupted boldly in front of her classmates and the judges, exactly as she had hoped, prompting enthusiastic applause and warm praise from her teacher for recognizing a problem, testing a solution, and persisting without giving up, precisely the approach, her teacher noted, that real scientists take toward their own work.

Later, one of the judges asked Layla what she had personally learned from the entire experience, prompting her to explain thoughtfully that scientists frequently fail several times before discovering the correct answer, and that adjusting even a single variable, such as the ratio of ingredients, can completely transform the final outcome. Her reflective, well-considered answer impressed the judges every bit as much as the eruption itself, demonstrating that the value of an experiment often lies as much in the careful process behind it as in its final, visible result.

keyWords.definition: a mountain that can shoot out hot melted rock, called lava, from inside the earth
keyWords.example: We watched a video about a volcano erupting far away.

keyWords.definition: two or more things combined together
keyWords.example: The paint mixture turned purple when we mixed red and blue.

keyWords.definition: a small round pocket of air or gas, often seen in a liquid
keyWords.example: Bubbles floated up from the bottom of the fish tank.

keyWords.definition: to make a liquid flow out of a container
keyWords.example: Please pour the juice carefully into the glasses.

keyWords.definition: short for baking soda, a white powder used in cooking and in science experiments
keyWords.example: We used baking soda to clean the sink.

questions.stem: What is this story mostly about?
options: A girl who bakes a cake for a big neighborhood party
A girl's volcano fails, so she and her brother fix it in time
A boy who wins an important soccer game for his school team
A girl who gets lost at a very busy, crowded science fair
questions.why: The story tells how Layla's volcano mixture fails during a practice test and how she and Omar find and fix the problem before the fair.

wrong.A: The story is not about baking a cake.
wrong.C: The story does not describe a soccer game.
wrong.D: Layla does not get lost in the story.

questions.stem: What happened first in the story?
options: Layla and Omar tested the volcano at home the night before
Layla showed her volcano at the fair
The judges praised Layla's work
Layla wrote down the new mixture
questions.why: The rehearsal at home happened before the problem was found, the mixture was fixed, and the volcano was shown at the fair.

wrong.B: The fair happened after the rehearsal and the fix.
wrong.C: The judges praised Layla after the eruption worked at the fair.
wrong.D: Layla wrote down the mixture after the second test worked.

questions.stem: Why did the volcano only make a few weak bubbles at first?
options: Omar poured in cold water instead of vinegar
The volcano box was too small for the mixture
Layla used too little baking soda for the vinegar
Layla forgot to add the red food coloring
questions.why: Layla and Omar found that she had measured too little baking soda compared to the vinegar, so the mixture barely bubbled.

wrong.A: The story does not say Omar used cold water.
wrong.B: The size of the volcano is not the problem in the story.
wrong.D: Food coloring only changes the color, not whether it bubbles.

questions.stem: Who helped Layla find the problem?
options: Layla's teacher, who arrived the next day
A judge who was at the science fair
Layla's friend who sat next to her at school
Omar, Layla's brother, helped her find the problem
questions.why: Omar suggested checking the notes, and together they found the mistake in the recipe.

wrong.A: The teacher only saw the finished project at the fair.
wrong.B: The judges only saw the final eruption at the fair.
wrong.C: No friend from school appears in this part of the story.

questions.stem: Why did Layla and Omar do a rehearsal the night before the fair?
options: To have fun with vinegar and soda
To make sure the volcano would work before the real fair
To clean the kitchen table
To find a brand new science topic
questions.why: Testing the volcano the night before let Layla find and fix any problems before the real presentation.

wrong.A: The rehearsal was a serious test, not just for fun.
wrong.C: Cleaning the kitchen happened after the rehearsal, not as its purpose.
wrong.D: Layla already had her topic; she was testing it, not choosing it.

questions.stem: In the story, the word mixture means —
options: A loud, rumbling sound made deep inside a volcano
A careful drawing of a volcano made on plain paper
Different things, like baking soda and vinegar, combined together
A kind of shiny trophy given out at a school fair
questions.why: The mixture is the combination of baking soda, vinegar, and food coloring that Layla poured into the volcano.

wrong.A: A mixture is not a sound.
wrong.B: A mixture is not a drawing.
wrong.D: A mixture is not a trophy.

questions.stem: How did Layla feel before fixing the mixture compared to after?
options: Worried before fixing the mixture, confident after
Happy and excited before, then quite angry after
Excited and eager before, then very bored after
Scared before, and still just as scared after
questions.why: Layla felt sad and worried when the first test failed, but she felt much more confident once she and Omar fixed the mixture.

wrong.B: Layla was not angry after fixing the mixture; she felt confident.
wrong.C: Layla was not bored; she was worried and later confident.
wrong.D: Layla's fear changed to confidence after the fix.

questions.stem: Why did the author include the part where Layla and Omar test the volcano the night before the fair?
options: To show that the volcano never worked at all
To explain exactly how to build a cardboard volcano
To describe what Omar's bedroom looked like
To show how Layla found a problem and fixed it just in time
questions.why: The rehearsal scene shows the process Layla went through to notice a mistake and correct it before the real fair.

wrong.A: The volcano did work after Layla fixed the mixture.
wrong.B: The story does not give step-by-step building instructions.
wrong.C: Omar's bedroom is not described in the story.

LOW.prompt: Would you have wanted to do a rehearsal the night before the fair, like Layla and Omar did? Explain why or why not, using at least two facts from the story.
checklist: I clearly said what I think.
I used at least two facts from the story.
I wrote complete sentences with capital letters and periods.
LOW.modelAnswer: Yes, I would want to do a rehearsal like Layla did. In the story, her first test only made a few weak bubbles instead of a big eruption. If she had not tested it early, she would not have had time to find the problem and fix the mixture before the real fair.

keyWords.definition: one of the things used to make a mixture or recipe
keyWords.example: Flour is the main ingredient in bread.

keyWords.definition: the amount of one thing compared to the amount of another
keyWords.example: The ratio of boys to girls in our class is three to four.

keyWords.definition: a practice of something before the real event
keyWords.example: The school band held a rehearsal before the concert.

keyWords.definition: what happens at the end of an action or test
keyWords.example: The result of the race surprised everyone.

keyWords.definition: a series of steps taken to do or make something
keyWords.example: Baking bread is a process that takes several hours.

questions.stem: Which sentence best states the central idea of the story?
options: Layla completely gives up on her whole science project after just one failed test
Omar decides to build his own separate volcano project for the fair
Layla and Omar test her volcano, discover the mixture was wrong, and fix it before the fair
Layla easily wins first place at the fair with absolutely no problems at all
questions.why: The story centers on Layla and Omar finding and correcting the mistake in the volcano mixture before the fair.

wrong.A: Layla does not give up; she tries again.
wrong.B: Omar helps with Layla's project rather than building his own.
wrong.D: The story does not say Layla wins first place or has no problems.

questions.stem: What two ingredients did Layla mix to make her volcano erupt?
options: Baking soda and vinegar
Sugar and warm water
Salt and cooking oil
Flour and whole milk
questions.why: Layla mixed baking soda and vinegar, with red food coloring, to create the eruption.

wrong.B: Sugar and water do not appear in the story.
wrong.C: Salt and oil are not part of Layla's mixture.
wrong.D: Flour and milk are not part of Layla's mixture.

questions.stem: What did Layla and Omar do before changing the mixture?
options: They asked their teacher for a brand-new topic
They bought a brand-new volcano kit from the store
They simply gave up and went straight to sleep
They reviewed the recipe card together, ingredient by ingredient
questions.why: Before changing anything, Layla and Omar checked the recipe card carefully to find the mistake.

wrong.A: They kept the same topic and fixed the mixture instead.
wrong.B: They did not buy a new kit; they fixed their own mixture.
wrong.C: They did not give up; they kept working on the problem.

questions.stem: Why did the first rehearsal result in only weak bubbles instead of a big eruption?
options: The kitchen was too cold for the reaction
The ratio of baking soda to vinegar was wrong
Omar poured the mixture too slowly
The food coloring reacted badly with the soda
questions.why: Layla had used far too little baking soda compared to the vinegar, which caused a weak reaction.

wrong.A: The story does not mention the kitchen's temperature.
wrong.C: The speed of pouring is not given as the cause.
wrong.D: Food coloring only changes the color, not the strength of the bubbling.

questions.stem: Why do you think Layla and Omar held a rehearsal the night before the fair instead of waiting until the actual day?
options: They wanted extra time to find and fix any problems before it was too late
They needed practice talking in front of people
Their teacher required every student to rehearse
They had nothing else planned for that evening
questions.why: Testing early gave them time to notice the weak eruption and fix the mixture before the real presentation.

wrong.B: The rehearsal was about testing the volcano, not about public speaking.
wrong.C: The story does not say a rehearsal was required by a teacher.
wrong.D: The rehearsal had a clear purpose: checking that the project worked.

questions.stem: In the story, the word result means —
options: A kind of ingredient used in cooking
A plan made before an experiment even starts
What happens at the end of a test or experiment
A tool used to measure liquid
questions.why: The weak bubbles were the result, or outcome, of the first test with the wrong mixture.

wrong.A: A result is not an ingredient.
wrong.B: A plan made beforehand is not the same as a result.
wrong.D: A result is not a measuring tool.

questions.stem: How does the story mostly organize events?
options: It carefully compares two different volcano projects side by side
It follows the order events happened: the rehearsal, the problem, the fix, and the fair
It simply lists facts about volcanoes with no real story at all
It describes the kitchen in great detail before describing Layla
questions.why: The story moves in time order, from the failed rehearsal to finding the problem, fixing it, and succeeding at the fair.

wrong.A: Only one volcano project is described in the story.
wrong.C: The story follows Layla and Omar, not a list of volcano facts.
wrong.D: The story introduces Layla and her project before describing the kitchen scene.

questions.stem: What can you tell about Omar from how he acted when the first test failed?
options: He was angry at Layla for failing the first test
He refused to help and left the kitchen upset
He laughed at Layla's mistake instead of helping
He stayed calm and tried to help his sister solve the problem
questions.why: Omar suggested checking the notes calmly instead of getting upset, showing that he wanted to help Layla.

wrong.A: Omar did not act angry; he stayed calm.
wrong.B: Omar did not leave; he stayed and helped.
wrong.C: Omar did not laugh at Layla; he helped her fix the problem.

MID.prompt: Explain how Layla and Omar figured out what was wrong with the volcano mixture and how they fixed it. Use at least two details from the story.
checklist: I explained how they found the problem.
I explained how they fixed it.
I used at least two details from the story.
MID.modelAnswer: Layla and Omar found the problem by checking the recipe card line by line after the first rehearsal failed. They noticed that Layla had used too little baking soda compared to the vinegar. To fix it, they repeated the experiment with much more baking soda, and this time the mixture erupted exactly as Layla had hoped.

keyWords.definition: an idea that can be tested to explain why something happens
keyWords.example: The scientist tested her hypothesis about how plants grow in the dark.

keyWords.definition: a part of an experiment that can be changed, or that changes
keyWords.example: In the experiment, the amount of sunlight was the only variable.

keyWords.definition: to find an answer using numbers and math
keyWords.example: She used a calculator to calculate the total cost of the trip.

keyWords.definition: the quality of continuing to try, even when something is hard
keyWords.example: His persistence helped him finally learn to ride a bike.

keyWords.definition: to study something carefully in order to understand it
keyWords.example: The students analyzed the data from their experiment.

questions.stem: Which statement best captures the central idea of the story?
options: Careful testing and persistence helped Layla turn a failed rehearsal into a success
Science fairs are too stressful for any student to actually enjoy
Mistakes always end a young scientist's work for good, with no way back
Omar built the entire volcano project without his sister's help at all
questions.why: The story shows how testing, analyzing a problem, and persisting through a setback let Layla succeed at the fair.

wrong.B: The story shows Layla succeeding, not simply suffering stress.
wrong.C: Layla's mistake did not end her project; she corrected it.
wrong.D: Layla, not Omar, built and presented the project, with Omar helping.

questions.stem: What specific variable had Layla changed without realizing it?
options: The amount of red food coloring she used
The ratio of baking soda to vinegar in her mixture
The size of the cardboard volcano itself
The temperature of the kitchen that evening
questions.why: Layla had measured far too little baking soda compared to the vinegar, changing the ratio without meaning to.

wrong.A: The food coloring amount is not identified as the problem.
wrong.C: The size of the volcano is not mentioned as a variable.
wrong.D: The kitchen's temperature is not discussed in the story.

questions.stem: What was the direct cause of the eruption finally working during the second test?
options: Omar poured the vinegar instead of Layla
The judges arrived early to watch the rehearsal
Layla calculated and added a larger amount of baking soda
Layla switched to a completely different brand of vinegar
questions.why: Once Layla calculated and added more baking soda, the mixture reacted strongly and erupted as planned.

wrong.A: The story does not say Omar poured the vinegar instead of Layla.
wrong.B: The judges only watched the real fair, not the rehearsal.
wrong.D: The story does not mention switching vinegar brands.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about why Omar suggested analyzing the notes rather than giving up?
options: He wanted to take over the project completely himself
He thought the science fair would surely be canceled
He did not actually care whether the project worked at all
He believed the problem could likely be identified and corrected with careful thought
questions.why: Omar's calm suggestion to review the notes shows he believed the problem was solvable with careful analysis.

wrong.A: Omar helped Layla rather than taking over her project.
wrong.B: Nothing in the story suggests the fair might be canceled.
wrong.C: Omar's actions show that he cared about helping his sister succeed.

questions.stem: Based on the judge's question at the end, what does the judge seem to value most?
options: Understanding how Layla learned from testing, failing, and adjusting her experiment
Winning first place above every other student
Having a perfectly flawless volcano with no problems at all
The exact brand of baking soda that Layla happened to use
questions.why: The judge asked what Layla learned, suggesting that understanding the process mattered as much as the eruption itself.

wrong.B: The judge's question is about learning, not ranking students.
wrong.C: The judge's question shows interest in the problem Layla faced, not a flawless process.
wrong.D: The specific brand of baking soda is not what the judge asked about.

questions.stem: In the story, persistence most nearly means —
options: Giving up quickly after a single failed attempt
Continuing to try, even after facing a setback
Measuring ingredients with extreme precision
Feeling nervous before a big presentation
questions.why: Layla's persistence was shown when she and Omar kept working on the mixture after the first test failed.

wrong.A: Persistence is the opposite of giving up quickly.
wrong.C: Precise measuring is part of the story, but it is not what persistence means.
wrong.D: Feeling nervous is different from continuing to try.

questions.stem: Which lists these events in the order they happened?
options: The judges applaud first, then the rehearsal fails, and Layla forms a hypothesis
Layla recalculates the mixture, then the rehearsal fails, and the judges applaud
The rehearsal fails, Layla and Omar analyze the recipe, and the fair eruption later succeeds
The fair eruption succeeds first, the rehearsal fails later, and Omar helps clean up
questions.why: The rehearsal failed first, then Layla and Omar analyzed the recipe, Layla recalculated the mixture, and finally the eruption succeeded at the fair.

wrong.A: The judges applaud only after the fair eruption, which comes last.
wrong.B: Layla recalculates the mixture only after the rehearsal fails and the recipe is analyzed.
wrong.D: The fair eruption happens after the rehearsal fails, not before.

questions.stem: Why does the author include the judge's question near the end of the story?
options: To suggest that eruptions matter more than understanding science
To show that judges always ask difficult, unrelated questions
To explain exactly how real volcanoes form in nature
To highlight that the process of testing and adjusting is as important as the final result
questions.why: The judge's question draws attention to what Layla learned, showing that the scientific process matters as much as the eruption.

wrong.A: The story suggests understanding matters as much as the eruption, not more than it.
wrong.B: Only one judge's question is shown, and it connects directly to the story.
wrong.C: The story is about a model volcano project, not a lesson on real volcanoes.

HIGH.prompt: The story shows that failing a rehearsal can actually help someone succeed later. Do you agree or disagree with this idea? Support your answer with evidence from the story.
checklist: I supported my position with specific evidence from the story.
I addressed at least one point someone might make against my view.
HIGH.modelAnswer: I agree that failing a rehearsal can help someone succeed later. In the story, Layla's rehearsal revealed that her baking soda to vinegar ratio was wrong, and that early failure gave her time to analyze the problem and recalculate the mixture before the real fair. Someone might argue that failing is simply discouraging, but Layla's persistence shows that a timely failure can actually prevent a much bigger one in front of the judges.
